html:
SMTO-EXE-0069 — The clipboard on the Gateway computer is busy

GUID: ca7cd22d-85ef-5b11-955b-cdf3815c42f5
Slug: clipboard-busy
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: clipboard

What happened

  • Another program on the Gateway computer was holding the clipboard, or SMTO already had many clipboard steps running, so this copy or paste didn't happen.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a few seconds for other tasks that are copying or pasting on that Gateway to finish. The Gateway handles at most 32 clipboard steps at once and refuses more until some finish.
  2. On the Gateway computer, finish or close anything that may be holding the clipboard, such as a clipboard manager, a remote desktop window or a program in the middle of copying. On Windows only one program can open the clipboard at a time, and SMTO gives up after a few quick tries.
  3. Ask SMTO in the conversation to do the clipboard step again. This step didn't happen, so asking again won't copy or paste anything twice.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the copy or paste and reports the result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Gateway's name, to the person who manages it. Don't force-close programs on that computer that may hold someone's unsaved work.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The clipboard request was refused because the Gateway already had 32 active clipboard requests, or the Windows backend could not open the native clipboard within five attempts because another process held it.

What this means

  • The clipboard service reached thirty-two active requests or the Windows backend could not acquire the native clipboard within its bounded open attempts. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • The clipboard service reached thirty-two active requests or the Windows backend could not acquire the native clipboard within its bounded open attempts.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish Gateway admission capacity from a native clipboard lock; identify active owned requests before disrupting an application.

How to fix it

  • Wait for in-flight clipboard requests to finish, or find the process holding the Windows clipboard open (OpenClipboard contention, for example a clipboard manager or remote-desktop clipboard sync) and release it through that application's own controls. Then send a new explicit request; the refused call read and wrote nothing.
  • Let existing requests or the clipboard holder finish, then make a new explicit request if needed. Stop another application only through its authorized owning controls.

Retry and execution caution

  • Close the application holding the clipboard and make a new explicit request.

How to verify the fix

  • The existing holder or requests release access and a separately requested action is admitted.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain clipboard write or include content in diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
